3. Impact on Socio-Economic Environment
a. Residents
Many residents of the area will be affected by the project both during and after the execution period. Most noticeable is the relocation of 49 individual residents. Those relocated will become eligible for the assistance described in Part I. This assistance will lessen the effects of relocation, however, this activity remains a negative factor as it relates to the personal lives of the individuals involved in the relocation. The relocation of businesses will not be on the same personal basis, but will nevertheless involve a certain amount of inconvenience to individuals.
Relocation of individuals and businessmen within the projects redeveloped properties will also offset the disadvantage of relocation program for some. In some instances, individuals may welcome relocation. The opportunity to sell a flood damaged property and receive relocation benefits may be welcomed by a number of the displacees.
As noted in Part II, there are no non-whites included in the relocation workload.
b. Tax Base
The removal of properties from the tax register will adversely effect the property tax base of the City government, the County government and the Harrisburg School System.
The removal of properties will be both of a permanent and temporary nature. Those properties that become publicly owned land (open spaces, rights-of-way) will be permanently eliminated from the property tax rolls. Those acquired by the project and subsequently sold for redevelopment will be lost from the tax rolls while they remain under the ownership of the local government during the execution period of the project (up to a 5 year period). Over a period of time, the adverse effects of the tax base loss will gradually be offset by other factors inherent with the renewal process.
At some point in time the property values in the area will benefit from the renewal process and begin to increase. Land acquired for resale to developers will be sold and once again become part of the tax digest. As the land is redeveloped and new structures appear the tax digest will further benefit.
